## Alston Bridges Barbecue (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/alston-bridges-barbecue/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/alston-bridges-barbecue.json
id: alston-bridges-barbecue
aliases: Alston Bridges
facets: state=NC · status=open · founded=1955 · fuel=mixed · styles=lexington
region: The North Carolina Piedmont
what: The Shelby pork-shoulder house of the other Bridges family, on East Grover Street in Cleveland County, where Alston Bridges and his wife Mabel bought the property in 1955. Alston learned the trade from his brother-in-law Warner Stamey, managing Stamey's Log Cabin Barbecue in Lexington for two and a half years first. About fifty shoulders a day go through the kitchen; the tray is chopped or coarse-chopped pork with red slaw and hushpuppies. What is under the meat is disputed: three accounts describe electric cookers or gas, one promotional listing says wood-smoked.
story: Two Bridges families cook barbecue in Shelby and they are not related — a shared ancestor somewhere in the 1700s is as close as the local history will put them. Warner Stamey trained both Red Bridges and Alston Bridges in the 1940s, and Alston's apprenticeship is the documented one: he and Mabel moved to Lexington, he managed Stamey's Log Cabin Barbecue for two and a half years, and then they came to Shelby and bought 620 East Grover Street. The county history gives the year as 1955 and a visiting writer gives 1956. Alston died in 1970; his son Kent and Kent's wife Linda took it on, and the county history says Kent and Linda's children operate the business now. Our State found Alston's grandson Reid Bridges behind the counter in 2013, explaining the difference between chopped and coarse-chopped. The fuel is where the sources part. Our State wrote in 2013 that he starts the pork on electric cookers and finishes it in a pit. A visiting writer in March 2024 found the smoke missing and put it down to a move from pit to gas some years earlier. The NC Pork Council's listing calls it wood-smoked. Neither the Historic Barbecue Trail nor the Campaign for Real Barbecue lists the house, and both exclude gas and electric.
how: About fifty pork shoulders a day, from a short-shank cut the kitchen buys through a Gastonia distributor. Our State's account of the method has the pork starting on electric cookers and finishing in a pit. The meat is chopped or coarse-chopped to order and served with red slaw, the cabbage cut fine and dressed with the Piedmont dip, and hushpuppies. The menus read: Pigs are Beautiful.
today: Open at 620 East Grover Street, Shelby. Hours differ across three listings, and the restaurant's own site was posting a Labor Day closing and a September 8 return when read on September 16, 2026. Check before driving.
address: 620 E Grover St, Shelby, NC, 28150
geo: 35.30425, -81.5277 (street)
- kin → lexington (style): the style of its tray, cooked forty miles west of Lexington itself.
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): the cut — about fifty short-shank shoulders a day.
- kin → warner-stamey (person): his brother-in-law and teacher; Alston managed Stamey's Log Cabin Barbecue before opening here.
- kin → red-slaw (dish): the slaw on its tray, dressed with the dip.
- kin → red-bridges-barbecue-lodge (place): the other Bridges barbecue in Shelby, from another family Stamey also trained.
- not to be confused with red-bridges-barbecue-lodge: Two Bridges, one town, no relation closer than a possible common ancestor in the 1700s. Red Bridges Barbecue Lodge is on US 74 and burns hickory and oak; Alston Bridges is on East Grover Street and its fuel is disputed in the sources. Warner Stamey taught both men in the 1940s.
sources: s:web-clevelandcounty-history — Food & Eateries; s:web-ourstate-shelby-2013 — Tar Heel Town: Shelby; s:web-barbecuebros-alston-bridges-2024 — Alston Bridges is more than just 'the other Bridges'; s:web-alstonbridges — Alston Bridges Barbecue — official site; s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-16

## B's Barbecue (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/bs-barbecue/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/bs-barbecue.json
id: bs-barbecue
aliases: B's · B's Barbeque · B's Bar-B-Q
facets: state=NC · status=open · founded=1978 · fuel=charcoal · styles=eastern-nc
region: Eastern North Carolina
what: A whole-hog and chicken pit on the edge of Greenville, Pitt County, in a converted country store on a road the county named for it. Bill McLawhorn, the B, opened it in 1978 with his wife Peggy; their daughters Judy Drach, Tammy Godley and Donna McLawhorn have run it since his death in 2007. There is no telephone, no take-out menu and no closing time: the doors open at nine in the morning and shut when the day's barbecue and chicken are gone, usually early afternoon. Cash or check only. The line forms before opening.
story: Bill McLawhorn gave up farming in 1978 and bought a convenience store just inside Greenville's city limits; he and Peggy worked out the sauce together and cooked out back, selling up front. He refused a telephone — 'If you need me, come get me' — and the refusal outlasted him. Bob Garner wrote it up for Our State in 2012 as a place of red picnic tables and cafeteria-style counter service with no promise the food would still be there at noon. Judy Drach told the Southern Foodways Alliance in 2009 that the family could have built something bigger with more staff and a day off, 'but when you start doing all that, then it's like any other restaurant and that's not what we wanted it to be.' Bill died in 2007 and the sisters took it on. The pits were once wood-fired brick; after fires the family went over to charcoal, and the pigs go on around nine at night to be ready by nine in the morning. The county renamed the road B's Barbecue Road.
how: Whole hogs and chickens cook overnight over charcoal, the hogs going on about 9 p.m. The pork is chopped by hand, never ground, and dressed with the McLawhorns' vinegar sauce; the chicken is sold by the half or the whole bird. In 2016 Our State printed the board: barbecue dinner $7.75, sandwich $3.75, a pound $8.50, half a chicken $7, a whole one $11.50. The customer orders at the counter and eats at a picnic table or in the car.
today: Open Tuesday to Saturday from 9 a.m. until sold out, at 751 B's Barbecue Road, Greenville. No phone. Cash or check. Hours pattern from Our State (2012 and 2016); check before driving.
address: 751 B's Barbecue Rd, Greenville, NC, 27834
geo: 35.6209409, -77.4173525 (street)
- kin → eastern-nc (style): the style, in its plainest form: whole hog, vinegar sauce, chopped by hand.
- kin → whole-hog (pit): the cut, cooked overnight over charcoal rather than wood since the fires.
- kin → barbecue-chicken (dish): the other thing on the pit, sold by the half and the whole.
- kin → chopping-block (pit): where the pork is chopped by hand; the family says it is never ground.
- kin → sam-jones-bbq (place): the other Pitt County whole-hog house, across Greenville in Winterville, with a phone and a bar.
- kin → skylight-inn (place): the Ayden pit fifteen miles south that the press pairs it with.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): recorded Judy Drach's oral history in 2009.

- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/images/bs-barbecue/bs-barbecue-hogs-for-smoking-at-b-s-barbecue.jpg · Public domain · City of Greenville, North Carolina · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AHogs_for_smoking_at_B%27s_Barbecue.jpg

Pike, 10 Jun 2009; s:web-truecue-nc — True 'Cue NC — certified pits; s:web-barbecuebros-nc-trail — NC Historic Barbecue Trail

## Backyard BBQ Pit (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/backyard-bbq-pit/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/backyard-bbq-pit.json
id: backyard-bbq-pit
aliases: Backyard Barbecue Pit · The Backyard BBQ Pit
facets: state=NC · status=unknown · founded=2007 · fuel=wood · styles=
region: The North Carolina Piedmont
what: A Black-owned barbecue restaurant on N.C. 55, the Apex Highway, in southeast Durham, opened in April 2007 by Fabianne and Melvin Simmons, who bought a struggling restaurant and made it a neighborhood institution: chopped barbecue and sandwiches, ribs, smoked chicken and oxtails, cooked over wood coals and made from scratch. Its later years were hard — a $50,000 GoFundMe in 2023, a change of owners, eight months dark for renovations before a March 2024 reopening, and in April 2026 a report that it was weeks from closing unless a buyer came. Its status in September 2026 is not confirmed on this disk.
story: Melvin Simmons ran the pit for more than sixteen years, Fabianne with him, from the April 2007 opening through recessions and the pandemic. In 2023 the family asked the public for $50,000 to keep the doors open. The reports on disk then part: Spectacular Magazine wrote in April 2026 that Angela McLean had taken the restaurant over in 2023, while CBS 17 reported in March 2024 that Damien Holloway, as new owner, had redone 'every single thing in the building' — equipment, floors, walls, ceilings, bathrooms — over eight closed months and was set to reopen, the grand opening slipping for weather. The Assembly, surveying the state's Black-owned pits in February 2026, found the restaurant exploring a sale, its future uncertain. By April 2026 McLean told Spectacular that customers were choosing between a meal and gas for the car, and that without a buyer the restaurant could close by the end of the month.
how: Barbecue chopped and sandwiched, ribs, smoked chicken and oxtails, cooked over wood coals and made from scratch, by the owners' accounts to the Durham press. Which cut, which sauce and which sides are not described in the sources on this disk, and no price is recorded.
today: Status unknown as of September 2026: the last reports on this disk, from February and April 2026, had it for sale and near closing. The address is 5122 N.C. Highway 55 (Apex Highway), Durham.
address: 5122 Apex Hwy, Durham, NC, 27713
geo: 35.89406, -78.89769 (street)
- kin → chopped (term): chopped barbecue was the first line of its menu.
- kin → barbecue-sandwich (dish): the sandwich, with ribs and oxtails beside it.
- kin → gradys-barbecue (place): the other Black-owned pit The Assembly surveyed in 2026, cooking whole hog in Wayne County.
- kin → adrian-miller (person): whose Black Smoke is the frame the press used for it: a Black-owned pit and what it takes to keep one.

## Bar-B-Q Center (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/bar-b-q-center/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/bar-b-q-center.json
id: bar-b-q-center
aliases: The Barbecue Center · Barbecue Center · Lexington Barbecue Center
facets: state=NC · status=open · founded=1955 · fuel=wood · styles=lexington
region: The North Carolina Piedmont
what: A pork-shoulder pit and ice-cream counter on North Main Street in Lexington, Davidson County, that began in 1955 as a dairy bar, put a shoulder on a pit one slow winter, and has been the Conrad family's since: Sonny Conrad (1938–2013), who started on curb service there as a teenager in 1955 and became owner in 1969, his wife Nancy, and their sons Michael and Cecil. Shoulders cook over hickory; the barbecue comes chopped, sliced or 'brown' — the smoky outside of the shoulder — with the dip and red slaw. The ice cream never left: about 200 gallons a week, much of it in a banana split of three and a half pounds.
story: The dairy bar of 1955 sold ice cream on Main Street, and in the 1960s the strip was a cruising street for hot rods; Sonny Conrad later put up metal railings to keep the place a family one, Our State wrote in 2014. Ice cream sales dip in winter, so one winter a pork shoulder went on a pit, and the restaurant's own history says it moved to its present building at 900 North Main in the late 1950s. Conrad had begun as a curb-service boy in 1955; in 1969 he married Nancy, a waitress there, and became the owner. He told the Southern Foodways Alliance in November 2011 that the kitchen made a hundred gallons a week each of dip and red slaw, that four customers in ten still ate in their cars, and that 'red slaw. That's a good vegetable.' He died in 2013; Nancy still worked, and the sons ran the day to day. Southern Living and Good Morning America have both come for the banana split. New airtight pits went in around 2013, glowing orange with coals; the dining room seats about a hundred at booths and a counter.
how: Pork shoulders cook over hickory coals with the family's spice blend; the meat is chopped or sliced, or served brown from the smoky outside, with the Lexington dip — thin, vinegar-based, reddened with ketchup — and red slaw, hushpuppies, baked beans and cornbread. Curb service brings the tray to the car. The banana split weighs three and a half pounds and is built for a table.
today: Open Monday to Saturday 11 to 9, at 900 North Main Street, Lexington, per OpenStreetMap (2026), which tags the address to Thomasville in error; the 27292 postcode and the restaurant's own site say Lexington. Dine-in and curb service.
address: 900 N Main St, Lexington, NC, 27292
geo: 35.83159, -80.2443 (street)
- kin → lexington (style): the style, with the town's largest curb-service trade and a dairy bar's dessert.
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): the cut, over hickory.
- kin → outside-brown (dish): 'brown' here is the smoky outside of the shoulder, ordered by name.
- kin → lexington-dip (sauce): a hundred gallons a week of it, by Sonny Conrad's count in 2011.
- kin → red-slaw (dish): a hundred gallons a week; 'that's a good vegetable.'
- kin → hushpuppies (dish): on the plate with baked beans and cornbread.
- kin → hickory-and-oak (pit): hickory, in airtight pits installed around 2013.
- kin → lexington-barbecue (place): the Monk family's pit across town, the other name visitors come with.
- kin → cooks-barbecue (place): the small brick-pit house south of town, closed since 2022.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): recorded Sonny Conrad two years before his death.

## Bessinger's Bar-B-Q (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/bessingers-bar-b-q/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/bessingers-bar-b-q.json
id: bessingers-bar-b-q
aliases: Bessinger's BBQ · Bessinger's Bar-Be-Que · Bessinger's Barbeque · Piggy Park Drive-In · Bessinger's — The Barbecue Family
facets: state=SC · status=open · founded=1960 · styles=sc-mustard
region: The Lowcountry, South Carolina
what: A Bessinger family barbecue house at 1602 Savannah Highway in Charleston's West Ashley. Thomas Bessinger came from Holly Hill to Charleston with his brother Melvin in 1955, opened his own restaurant in 1960, and in 1961 the brothers opened Piggy Park Drive-In on the highway; renamed Bessinger's in 1971, it is run by Thomas's sons Tommy and Michael. It serves chopped pork in the family's mustard sauce, ribs, hash and rice, and a buffet on weekend evenings, and the South Carolina Barbeque Association lists it as 100-Mile Barbecue — a house worth a hundred-mile drive. It is the Charleston branch of the family whose Columbia branch is Maurice's Piggie Park.
story: Joseph Jacob 'Big Joe' Bessinger traded the family cow, a mule and fifty dollars for the Holly Hill Café in 1939 and served mustard-sauced barbecue there. After the war his son Melvin put his Army pay into a second Holly Hill restaurant, Eat At Joe's, in 1946, and the younger Thomas — born in Orangeburg in 1931 — started cooking there at fourteen. Thomas joined the Army after school and cooked two years overseas for soldiers. In 1955 Melvin closed Eat At Joe's and moved to Charleston, bringing Thomas; Thomas opened his own restaurant there in 1960, and in 1961 the brothers opened Piggy Park Drive-In on Savannah Highway together. After ten years they renamed it Bessinger's — The Barbecue Family. In 1982 Melvin crossed the Cooper River to open Melvin's in Mount Pleasant, and the brothers went their own ways. When their brother Maurice raised Confederate flags over his Columbia restaurants in July 2000, the press described the Charleston brothers' businesses as independent concerns, 'sans the politics'; grocery chains that dropped Maurice's sauce stocked Melvin's, and Maurice stopped speaking to him. Thomas Bessinger Sr. died on November 10, 2023, at ninety-two, with the restaurant in his sons' hands.
how: Chopped pork dressed in the family's yellow mustard sauce, from a pit behind the building; ribs, St. Louis cut, wet with the same sauce; hash over rice that the Barbeque Association's listing rates 'very, very good'; and onion rings the size of a doughnut. The buffet runs Friday and Saturday evenings and Sunday midday.
today: Open seven days, 10:30 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., with the buffet Friday and Saturday 5:30 to 8:30 p.m. and Sunday noon to 8, per the Barbeque Association's listing; OpenStreetMap recorded 11 to 9 in November 2023. 1602 Savannah Highway, Charleston. Checked September 15, 2026.
address: 1602 Savannah Hwy, Charleston, SC, 29407
geo: 32.78697, -80.01177 (street)
- kin → sc-mustard (style): the style it carried from the Midlands to the coast in 1955.
- kin → mustard-sauce (sauce): the sauce Big Joe worked out in Holly Hill, served here since the drive-in years.
- kin → joe-bessinger (person): the father, whose Holly Hill Café of 1939 is where the sons learned.
- kin → maurice-bessinger (person): Thomas's brother; his flags of 2000 were his own, and the Charleston houses were reported as separate concerns.
- kin → maurices-piggie-park (place): the West Columbia chain of the same family and sauce; a separate business.
- kin → sweatmans-bar-b-que (place): the Holly Hill family that worked on the mustard sauce with Big Joe.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): on the menu and the buffet; the Association's reviewer rated it 'very, very good'.
- kin → home-team-bbq (place): the newer West Ashley barbecue, opened in 2006 about a mile away on Ashley River Road.
- kin → south-carolina-barbeque-association (org): lists it as 100-Mile Barbecue.
- not to be confused with maurices-piggie-park: Bessinger's is the Charleston house, Thomas's since 1960; Maurice's Piggie Park is the West Columbia chain since 1953. Same father, same sauce, separate businesses — and Maurice's is the one with the court case and the flags.
sources: s:web-melvins-our-story — Our Story — Melvin's BBQ; s:web-live5-thomas-bessinger-2023 — Bessingers BBQ announces passing of family patriarch (November 11, 2023); s:web-abc4-thomas-bessinger-2023 — Thomas Bessinger Sr. 'patriarch' of Bessingers BBQ dead at 92 (November 2023); s:web-top100bbq-bessingers — Bessinger's Bar-Be-Que — 100-Mile Barbecue listing; s:web-barbecuetricks-bessingers — Bessinger's BBQ — South Carolina; s:web-charleston-mag-mustard-migration — The Mustard-Sauce Migration — the evolution of Charleston barbecue, part 1; s:web-sfa-melvins-legendary-bar-b-q — Melvin's Legendary Bar-B-Q — David Bessinger, interviewed by Rien Fertel, June 26, 2012; s:web-baltimore-sun-bessinger-2002 — S.C. barbecue king stands his ground (September 22, 2002); s:web-seattle-times-piggie-park-2002 — Confederate flag still flies over Piggie Park — Ariel Sabar (October 5, 2002); s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina

## Big T Bar-B-Q (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/big-t-bar-b-q/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/big-t-bar-b-q.json
id: big-t-bar-b-q
aliases: Big T's Bar-B-Que · Big T's
facets: state=SC · status=open · fuel=wood · styles=
region: The South Carolina Midlands
what: A Black-owned wood-burning pit on Congaree Road at Gadsden, in lower Richland County below Columbia, run by Larry Brown, known as Teddy and as Big T, who has sold barbecue to the Columbia area for more than thirty years. Logs burn down in a warped burn box behind the smokehouse and the coals are shovelled into low metal pits under pork shoulders. Hash goes over rice, made with pork and offal in the Midlands way. A second house on Garners Ferry Road in Columbia serves the same barbecue from a buffet.
story: Neither the founding year nor a founding date is on this disk; what the listings agree on is that Larry Brown has been at it in this part of Richland County for over thirty years. He is not a Sweatman, and Big T has no connection to Sweatman's Bar-B-Que at Holly Hill, though the two names travel together in loose accounts of South Carolina barbecue. The evidence that the business is Black-owned is the directory kind rather than the profile kind: EatOkra, which indexes Black-owned restaurants, carries it, and the chef Todd Richards put it in his guide to Black-owned barbecue. A 2019 newspaper profile that would have said it in a reporter's words could not be fetched for this record. The South Carolina Barbeque Association's own page files Big T under Worth the Trip and describes the method — slow over coals and wood at the Gadsden operation — while saying the hash there is a little mild for the writer's taste, which is the sort of judgement a project like this one records rather than adopts. Brown's son Travis works the pits. The Gadsden house closes Sunday, Monday and Tuesday; the Columbia house runs a buffet.
how: Logs burn down to coals in a large warped burn box behind the smokehouse, and the coals are shovelled into low metal pits under pork shoulders — not whole hogs. The hash is the Midlands kind, pork and offal cooked down and ladled over white rice. Cards and cash are both taken. The Garners Ferry Road house in Columbia serves from a buffet; Gadsden does not.
today: Open at 2520 Congaree Road, Gadsden, closed Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, with a second house at 7535 Garners Ferry Road, Columbia. The map point is the Congaree Road centreline rather than the building: the geocoder returned the road, not the house number.
address: 2520 Congaree Rd, Gadsden, SC, 29052
geo: 33.8552, -80.76565 (street)
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): the cut: shoulders over shovelled coals, not whole hogs.
- kin → burn-barrel (pit): the principle of its fire, here a warped burn box behind the smokehouse.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): the Midlands plate it serves — pork and offal cooked down, over white rice.
- kin → campaign-for-real-barbecue (org): certified both its houses as cooking on wood or charcoal alone.
- kin → south-carolina-barbeque-association (org): files it under Worth the Trip and describes the coals-and-wood method at Gadsden.
- kin → adrian-miller (person): wrote the history of African American barbecue that the Black-owned directories sit downstream of.
- not to be confused with sweatmans-bar-b-que: No relation. Sweatman's is Harold 'Bub' Sweatman's whole-hog house at Holly Hill in Orangeburg County, opened 1977 and sold twice since. Big T is Larry Brown's shoulder pit at Gadsden in Richland County. Loose accounts sometimes attach a Sweatman surname to Big T; no source read here does.
sources: s:web-destination-bbq-big-t — Big T's Bar-B-Que Restaurant in Gadsden, SC; s:web-top100bbq-big-t — Big T's Bar-B-Q; s:web-eatokra-big-t — Big T's Bar-B-Que — EatOkra listing; s:web-eatokra — EatOkra — a directory of Black-owned restaurants; s:web-truecue-sc — True 'Cue SC — certified pits; s:web-destination-bbq-hash-map — The South Carolina BBQ Hash Map; s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina

## Bobbee O's BBQ (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/bobbee-os-bbq/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/bobbee-os-bbq.json
id: bobbee-os-bbq
aliases: Bobbee O's
facets: state=NC · status=open · founded=2008 · fuel=unknown · styles=
region: The North Carolina Piedmont
what: A Black-owned barbecue counter on Statesville Road in north Charlotte, opened in 2008 by Bob Steven Roberts after four years working on his sauce. The board runs to pulled pork, ribs, brisket and wings rather than whole hog, and the room is counter service with online ordering. Roberts's niece Chloria Chandler is his business partner. It is one of the few barbecue businesses in Mecklenburg County that the Black-owned business directories carry, and the only one in this project's Charlotte records.
story: Bob Steven Roberts spent four years on the sauce before he opened. He had lived in California and New Jersey before coming to North Carolina more than thirty years ago, cooked in Fayetteville and Raleigh, and landed in Charlotte. His niece Chloria Chandler works with him as his business partner; she told QCity Metro in November 2021 that her favourite is the ribs, because she had been eating them since she was in her mother's stomach. The Black-owned business directories carry him: EatOkra lists the restaurant, NBA.com put it first in a list of ten Black-owned Charlotte restaurants in February 2023, and the chef Todd Richards included it in his guide to Black-owned barbecue, updated May 2025, with a note that this is the place for a sampler plate. What is under the meat is not settled. A 2024 lifestyle listing says hickory; a barbecue blog reported second-hand in 2016 that the kitchen ran a cabinet smoker and was not trying for wood smoke, and its own 2012 visit found no smoker in sight. The restaurant's site says nothing about fuel, so no wood tag is set here. *Inference —* the sauce, not the fire, is what every account of this kitchen is actually about.
how: Counter service and online ordering: pulled pork, ribs, brisket and wings by the plate or the pound, with the house sauce that took four years to settle. There is no whole hog on the board in any source read, and no hash. Cards are taken. The room keeps long hours by barbecue standards, into the evening six nights and to eight on Sunday.
today: Open, on the listings read, at 9401 Statesville Road, Suite C, Charlotte; an earlier address on Old Statesville Road appears in accounts from 2012. No closure notice was found and no news-grade source confirms trading in 2026, so treat the status as reported rather than checked.
address: 9401 Statesville Rd, Suite C, Charlotte, NC, 28269
geo: 35.34873, -80.84135 (street)
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): the cut behind its pulled pork; there is no whole hog on the board.
- kin → barbecue-sandwich (dish): the plate most of its accounts describe, with the sauce that took four years.
- kin → adrian-miller (person): wrote the book on African American barbecue that frames why a directory of Black-owned pits exists at all.
sources: s:web-qcitymetro-bobbee-os — At this Black-owned restaurant, a BBQ recipe four years in the making; s:web-nba-black-owned-charlotte — 10 Black-owned restaurants to visit in Charlotte; s:web-eatokra-bobbee-os — Bobbee O's BBQ — EatOkra listing; s:web-eatokra — EatOkra — a directory of Black-owned restaurants; s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina
provenance default: cited · confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-16

## Bobby's BBQ (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/bobbys-bbq/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/bobbys-bbq.json
id: bobbys-bbq
aliases: Bobby's
facets: state=SC · status=open · founded=2018 · fuel=wood · styles=
region: The Upstate
what: A Texas-leaning smokehouse on North Main Street in Fountain Inn, Greenville County, owned by Octavius Nelson, called Tay, and his wife Sarah. Brisket, pulled pork, ribs, turkey and house-made sausage come off the pits; there is no hash and no buffet, which sets it apart from most South Carolina barbecue houses. The name is for Tay's father Bobby Nelson Sr. and his brother Bobby Jr., both dead before the business began. A seasoning line came first, in 2010; the restaurant followed.
story: Tay Nelson started working with his father in a Greenville restaurant at twelve. Bobby Nelson Sr. died in 2008 and Bobby Jr. in 2009, and what Tay built next was assembled out of what they left him: he blended a seasoning from the spices his father had used, sold it from 2010, and taught himself to smoke from tutorials on the internet. The restaurant opened in 2018, though the business's own page dates the barbecue side to 2014 and the seasoning to 2010, so the anniversary depends on which thread is counted. The ownership line is unusually plain, in the business's own words: Bobby's BBQ is owned by Tay Nelson and his wife Sarah. That is the sentence the woman-owned tag here rests on. What the record does not carry is a Black-owned tag. Nothing on the business's own pages uses the phrase, EatOkra does not list it, and a Post and Courier piece that might have settled it returned an error on two attempts. The press the business does have is broad and national — ABC News in 2020, Tamron Hall in 2021, a Forbes gift guide, a Google economic impact report — rather than the barbecue-world kind.
how: Brisket, pulled pork, ribs, turkey and house-made sausage, in the Central Texas manner rather than the Midlands one: no hash on the menu, no mustard tradition, no buffet. The seasoning blend that started the business in 2010 is still sold. Cards and cash are both taken. The kitchen runs four days, Thursday to Saturday, and the smoke is wood, on the strength of the certification rather than any published description of the fire.
today: Open Thursday to Saturday, 11 a.m. to 8 p.m., closed Sunday to Wednesday, at 1301 North Main Street, Fountain Inn. Both the restaurant's own site and the OpenStreetMap harvest agree on the address.
address: 1301 N Main St, Fountain Inn, SC, 29644
geo: 34.70625, -82.22974 (street)
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): the cut behind its pulled pork, beside a Texas board of brisket and sausage.
- kin → campaign-for-real-barbecue (org): certified the pit as cooking on wood or charcoal alone.
- kin → lewis-barbecue (place): the other Carolina house built on Central Texas method rather than a local one, three hours east in Charleston.

## Brown's Bar-B-Que (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/browns-bar-b-que/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/browns-bar-b-que.json
id: browns-bar-b-que
aliases: Brown's Bar-B-Q · Brown's BBQ · Brown's
facets: state=SC · status=open · founded=1981 · styles=sc-pee-dee
region: The Pee Dee, South Carolina
what: A farm family's buffet house on the Williamsburg County Highway north of Kingstree, in the Pee Dee, opened in 1981 as a take-out window by Thomas M. Brown Jr., a row-crop farmer, with a dining room added about ten years on. Whole hogs are cooked and chopped, mopped on the pit with a vinegar-and-hot-pepper sauce the family calls barbecue gravy, and set on a long buffet with ribs, smoked ham, barbecued and fried chicken, barbecued and baked turkey, perloo, liver hash and rice, and vegetables the Browns grow themselves — corn, squash, okra, butter beans, collards, cabbage. The Barbeque Association names it among the state's top barbecue houses.
story: Thomas Brown learned to cook as a teenager laid up after a motorcycle accident broke his leg, working a hot plate within reach of the bed. He farmed — soy, wheat, hay and oats for market — and in 1981 opened a take-out window on the highway; the dining room came a decade later. The farm feeds the buffet: corn, squash, zucchini, broccoli, okra, butter beans, collards and cabbage in season. When the Southern Foodways Alliance came through the Pee Dee in June 2012, Rien Fertel recorded the Browns, and Angela Brown told him, 'We always take barbecue everywhere we go.' Kingstree is a whole-hog town — its Pig Pickin' festival each fall draws cooking teams, seventy of them in 2010, to compete on the county's vinegar-based barbecue — and Brown's is its standing barbecue house, more than forty years on. In April 2024 a visiting writer paid $14.95 for the buffet and ate liver hash over rice with salt, pepper and Texas Pete.
how: Whole hogs on the pit, mopped as they cook with the barbecue gravy — vinegar and hot pepper — then chopped. The buffet runs the length of the room: chopped barbecue, ribs, smoked ham, barbecued and fried chicken, barbecued and baked turkey, perloo (rice cooked with chicken), white rice, liver hash — hash with the liver in it, as the name says — macaroni, sweet potatoes, coleslaw, potato salad, the farm's vegetables, a salad bar and pecan pie. Buffet $14.95 in April 2024; a whole-hog plate with bread, baked beans and slaw is the take-out order.
today: Open Wednesday to Saturday 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and Sunday 11 to 3, closed Monday and Tuesday, per Destination BBQ; 809 North Williamsburg County Highway (US 52), Kingstree. Checked September 15, 2026.
address: 809 N Williamsburg County Hwy, Kingstree, SC, 29556
geo: 33.6943268, -79.8181123 (street)

- kin → whole-hog (pit): the cut, mopped as it cooks and chopped for the line.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): liver hash here, over white rice.
- kin → chicken-bog (dish): its perloo is the same chicken-and-rice under the Pee Dee name.
- kin → texas-pete (sauce): on the table for the hash.
- kin → pig-pickin (event): Kingstree's fall Pig Pickin' festival is the competitive form of what Brown's cooks all year.
- kin → mccabes-bar-b-q (place): the Manning buffet forty minutes west, the same whole-hog-and-vegetables form.
- kin → coopers-country-store (place): the country store seven miles south on US 521 that cooks whole hogs for its meat counter.
- kin → scotts-bar-b-que (place): the Hemingway pit twenty miles east; the two are the county's whole-hog names.
- kin → south-carolina-barbeque-association (org): names it among the state's top barbecue houses.

## Bum's Restaurant (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/bums-restaurant/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/bums-restaurant.json
id: bums-restaurant
aliases: Bum's · Bum's Barbecue · Bum's Restaurant Ayden
facets: state=NC · status=open · founded=1963 · fuel=wood · styles=eastern-nc
region: Eastern North Carolina
what: A wood-fired whole-hog restaurant in downtown Ayden, Pitt County, opened in 1963 by Latham 'Bum' Dennis, of the family that counts Skilton Dennis's 1830 wagon as the start of barbecue for sale here, and run by his son Larry, who cuts the wood, burns the coals and starts around four in the morning. Unlike most eastern pits it keeps a buffet of vegetables cooked that day — collards from the family garden, cabbage pastry, stewed rutabaga, black-eyed peas, boiled potatoes — beside the chopped barbecue. The sign is modest; the smell does the advertising.
story: Latham Dennis opened Bum's in 1963. The family's claim runs back to Skilton Dennis, who *tradition holds —* sold smoked hog meat commercially from 1830, a date the Southern Foodways Alliance recorded from the Dennises themselves, and to Otter Dennis, whom the family connects to the founding of Ayden; the Skylight Inn's Joneses paint the same 1830 on their billboard. Bum told the Alliance's Rien Fertel in December 2011, with Larry beside him, that in this kind of restaurant 'what you got to do you got to love it and it's a way of life.' Our State in April 2014 found Larry cutting oak and pecan and burning it down to embers before dawn, and Shirley Dennis, the family's matriarch, decorating the overflow dining room with Gone with the Wind memorabilia, a parking space reserved for her outside. Bum Dennis died in December 2022; Larry runs the restaurant. The vegetable buffet is what the writers single out: collards grown by the family, cabbage pastry, rutabaga, black-eyed peas, boiled potatoes, a table few other eastern pits keep.
how: Whole hogs cook over embers burned down from oak and pecan; the pork is chopped and dressed eastern-style, with vinegar and pepper. The barbecue is one station of a cafeteria line: the rest is the day's vegetables — collards from the family garden, cabbage pastry (cabbage stewed with strips of flat dumpling dough), rutabaga, black-eyed peas, boiled potatoes — and the plate is built by pointing.
today: Open, at 566 East Third Street, Ayden; Larry Dennis runs it. Hours are not recorded on this disk, and the last press confirmation read is from 2022; check before driving.
address: 566 E 3rd St, Ayden, NC, 28513
geo: 35.4709338, -77.4168893 (street)
- kin → eastern-nc (style): the style, with a vegetable table most eastern pits do not keep.
- kin → whole-hog (pit): the cut, over oak and pecan embers.
- kin → bum-dennis (person): its founder, at the pit from 1963 until his death in December 2022.
- kin → skilton-dennis (person): the ancestor whose 1830 wagon the family counts as the start of the trade.
- kin → skylight-inn (place): the other Ayden pit, five minutes away, which claims the same Dennis root.
- kin → sam-jones-bbq (place): the Jones family's newer house in Winterville, the third whole-hog pit within a few miles.
- kin → boiled-potatoes (dish): on the buffet with the collards and the cabbage pastry.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): recorded Bum and Larry Dennis together in 2011.

## Buxton Hall Barbecue (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/buxton-hall-barbecue/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/buxton-hall-barbecue.json
id: buxton-hall-barbecue
aliases: Buxton Hall · Buxton Hall Bar-B-Cue
facets: state=NC · status=closed · founded=2015 · fuel=wood · styles=eastern-nc, sc-pee-dee
region: The North Carolina mountains
what: A whole-hog restaurant that ran from August 2015 to November 22, 2023 in a 1930s roller rink on Banks Avenue in Asheville's South Slope, opened by pitmaster Elliott Moss with Meherwan Irani's Chai Pani restaurant group. Pasture-raised pigs from western North Carolina farms smoked over wood from ten at night to eight in the morning; the plate carried South Carolina hash over rice — the pig's organs and fatty trimmings cooked down to a gravy — beside the chopped hog, with a fried-chicken sandwich, smoked baked beans and pimento cheese, lard-crust pies and banana pudding under meringue. The rink's murals stayed on the walls.
story: Elliott Moss grew up watching his grandfather smoke whole hogs, and brought that South Carolina whole hog to the mountains. He and Meherwan Irani, both James Beard nominees, opened Buxton Hall in August 2015 in a building that had been a roller rink in the 1930s and then the Standard Paper Sales Company. Bon Appétit ranked it ninth among the country's new restaurants in 2016 and named its fried chicken sandwich the sandwich of the year. The pandemic closed it from March to July 2020; a fire later forced another closure and new equipment. Moss left as pitmaster in July 2022 and chef Nick Barr took the kitchen. The Smoke Sheet reported on November 8, 2023 that the last day of service would be November 22. Chai Pani, Irani's Indian restaurant, moved from Battery Park Avenue into the 8,000-square-foot space and reopened there on May 21, 2024.
how: Whole hogs from pasture farms smoked overnight, ten to eight, over wood, then were chopped in the eastern way. The hash — organs and trimmings cooked to a gravy — went over rice as it does in the Pee Dee. The kitchen fried chicken for a sandwich, smoked the baked beans and the pimento cheese, baked pies on lard crusts and topped the banana pudding with meringue.
today: Closed since November 22, 2023. Chai Pani, its co-owner's Indian restaurant, has occupied the rink at 32 Banks Avenue, Asheville, since its reopening there on May 21, 2024.
address: 32 Banks Ave, Asheville, NC, 28801
geo: 35.5890734, -82.5533593 (street)
- kin → eastern-nc (style): the chopped whole hog was cooked the eastern way, in a city that had not had one.
- kin → sc-pee-dee (style): the hash over rice came from Moss's South Carolina; the two Carolinas shared one plate here.
- kin → whole-hog (pit): the cut, pasture-raised, overnight over wood.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): on the plate, made from the hog's organs and trimmings.
- kin → elliott-moss (person): its founding pitmaster, who left in July 2022, fifteen months before it closed.
- kin → banana-pudding (dish): under meringue, the house version.
sources: s:web-ourstate-buxton-hall — Buxton Hall Barbecue Brings Whole-Hog Tradition and Hash to Asheville — Our State; s:web-smokesheet-buxton-hall-closes — Buxton Hall Barbecue closes — The Smoke Sheet (8 Nov 2023); s:web-wlos-chai-pani — Chai Pani holds colorful grand reopening at new location — WLOS (21 May 2024)

## Cannon's BBQ (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/cannons-bbq/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/cannons-bbq.json
id: cannons-bbq
aliases: Cannons BBQ · Cannons BBQ & More · Cannon's
facets: state=SC · status=closed · fuel=wood · styles=sc-mustard
region: The South Carolina Midlands, South Carolina
what: A small barbecue house in a converted mobile home at a five-way crossroads in Little Mountain, Newberry County — the Dutch Fork, the German-settled land between the Broad and Saluda rivers where the Midlands mustard sauce is at home. The Cannons cooked over wood coals they burned down themselves and chopped the pork for a sauce with a concentrated yellow-mustard taste; the ribs fell off the bone, and the hash — the Midlands' stew of pork and onion, here tinged bright yellow with mustard — is what Robert Moss remembered it for. It has closed: Moss, writing in March 2020, called it recently closed.
story: Little Mountain sits off Interstate 26 at exit 91, and Cannon's sat a few miles from the exit in a modified mobile home at a 'five points' intersection, with an overfilled dumpster and wood strewn about the lot when Destination BBQ came in March 2014 — the wood being the point, since the Cannons burned their own coals. The reviewers found the pork chopped finer than they liked, the ribs falling off the bone, the hash good and the sauce 'typical of the Midlands: mustard based', with a very concentrated yellow-mustard flavor. Robert Moss, telling the story of hash and rice in 2020, used it as his example of the mustard-yellow hash: 'At the recently-closed Cannon's BBQ in Little Mountain, S.C., the hash was tinged bright yellow with mustard.' *Tradition holds —* the Cannon brothers ran it about fifteen years and served the last plates on July 4, 2019, a closing the Columbia station WLTX reported that June.
how: Pork chopped and sauced with a yellow-mustard sauce, ribs that fell from the bone, and hash — pork and onion cooked down to a spoonable stew — tinged bright yellow with mustard and served over rice, all cooked over wood coals the family burned down on the lot. The building was a mobile home fitted out as a dining room, the lot a woodyard.
today: Closed. Robert Moss described it as recently closed in March 2020; no reopening is recorded in this project's sources as of September 15, 2026. The coordinates here are the town's, not the building's.
address: Little Mountain, SC, 29075
geo: 34.1962557, -81.4123229 (town)
- kin → sc-mustard (style): its style: Dutch Fork mustard, in the sauce and in the hash.
- kin → mustard-sauce (sauce): its sauce, with a concentrated yellow-mustard taste.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): its hash was the mustard-yellow kind, the one Moss chose as his example.
- kin → dutch-fork (term): the country it stood in: German-settled land between the Broad and the Saluda, home ground of the mustard sauce.
- kin → robert-moss (person): the historian who used its hash as his example of the Midlands' mustard-tinged kind.
- kin → hites-bar-b-q (place): the nearest open kettle-hash house of the same style, in West Columbia.

## Carolina Bar-B-Que (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/carolina-bar-b-que/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/carolina-bar-b-que.json
id: carolina-bar-b-que
aliases: Carolina BBQ · Carolina Bar-B-Que of New Ellenton
facets: state=SC · status=open · founded=1969 · fuel=wood · styles=sc-mustard
region: The South Carolina Midlands
what: A mustard-sauce buffet house on South Main Street in New Ellenton, Aiken County, founded by Willie Mae Walker and her son Jess. She was born Willie Mae Baltzegar, daughter of the Rowesville pitmaster Willie Baltzegar, which puts a pit-cooking line behind the place two generations deep. Pork shoulders cook over wood in smokers out back — not open-pit whole hog. The buffet was twelve dollars in April 2025 and the hash is rust-orange and thick enough to lift on a fork. Thomas Zeigler has run it since about 2022.
story: Willie Mae Walker came out of Rowesville, where her father Willie Baltzegar cooked, and she and her son Jess opened in New Ellenton — 1969 by two accounts, 1968 by a third. Naming her as a founder is not a courtesy: the sources put her first, with her son second, which is unusual enough in this trade to be worth saying once. Jess 'Bubba' Walker carried it on. Then the place slipped. Michael Stern, writing for The Food Section on April 22, 2025, said it had been losing its footing four or five years earlier — the food not up to standard and the staff getting cranky — before Thomas Zeigler took the business over about three years before he wrote, tweaked a few recipes and turned it round. Destination BBQ's page, updated April 2025, still names Bubba Walker as the owner, so the two listings disagree and the later, purpose-built piece is followed here. Southern Living put it on the South's Top 50 barbecue list in 2016, a list Robert Moss compiled, and the Barbeque Association gives it the hundred-mile designation. The Campaign for Real Barbecue certified it. Destination BBQ traces the hash recipe to the Dukes family tradition, which is the Orangeburg line reaching west.
how: Pork shoulders only — no ribs — cook over wood in smokers behind the building, which is not the open-pit whole-hog method of the Pee Dee and is described that way by the writers who visit. The sauce is the Midlands mustard. The buffet is all you can eat, twelve dollars in April 2025. The hash is rust-orange, thick, with an organ-meat sweetness, ladled over rice; one writer put it slightly thicker than Maurice's and a little less tart.
today: Open Wednesday 11 to 1:30 and Thursday to Saturday 11 to 8, closed Sunday to Tuesday, at 109 South Main Street, New Ellenton. Cards and cash. A search result circulating a South Main address in the eight hundreds is not supported by any page read here.
address: 109 S Main St, New Ellenton, SC, 29809
geo: 33.4186, -81.68524 (street)
- kin → sc-mustard (style): the sauce belt it sits in, west of Orangeburg on the Savannah River side.
- kin → mustard-sauce (sauce): its sauce, the Midlands yellow one.
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): the cut — shoulders only, and no ribs.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): its rust-orange hash over rice, traced to the Dukes family tradition.
- kin → dukes-bar-b-que (place): the Orangeburg family whose hash tradition a listing traces this one to.
- kin → campaign-for-real-barbecue (org): certified the pit as cooking on wood or charcoal alone.
- kin → robert-moss (person): compiled the 2016 Southern Living list of the South's top fifty barbecue houses that carried it.
sources: s:web-thefoodsection-carolina-bbq-2025 — Carolina Bar-B-Que shines again under new owner; s:web-southernflavor-sc-cue-2022 — Let's 'Meat' and Try Some New 'Cue; s:web-johntanner-carolina-bbq-2024 — Carolina Bar-B-Que, New Ellenton, South Carolina; s:web-carolina-bbq-new-ellenton — Carolina Bar-B-Que, New Ellenton — listing; s:web-truecue-sc — True 'Cue SC — certified pits; s:web-destination-bbq-hash-map — The South Carolina BBQ Hash Map; s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina

## Clyde Cooper's BBQ (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/clyde-coopers/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/clyde-coopers.json
id: clyde-coopers
aliases: Clyde Cooper's Barbecue · Clyde Cooper's · Cooper's
facets: state=NC · status=open · founded=1938 · fuel=unknown · styles=eastern-nc, lexington
region: Eastern North Carolina
what: Raleigh's downtown barbecue house since New Year's Day 1938, when Clyde Cooper opened on East Davie Street with fifty dollars borrowed from a brother-in-law; it moved around the corner to 327 South Wilmington Street in 2014 when the old building was lost to development, carrying the awning and the front door with it. It cooks pork shoulders — hand-trimmed, never whole hog — in pits on the upper floor, chops them and dresses them with Cooper's tangy sauce, which the city's tourism office calls a blend of eastern and Lexington ways. Fried chicken, Brunswick stew, collards, hushpuppies, boiled potatoes and banana pudding fill out the board; fried pork skins ride on the tray.
story: Clyde Cooper opened on January 1, 1938 in an 1884 building at 109 East Davie Street, and for fifty years he alone held the key. He cooked at first behind his house on Chapel Hill Road until the health department stopped him and the pits went upstairs, built to order by Nunnery-Freeman. The restaurant's own history says he was among the first Raleigh business owners to let Black customers in through the front door, in the early 1960s. After decades of being asked, he sold around 1988 to a builder named Tony; Debbie Holt, who had managed the place for him for five and a half years, took it over around 2008. Clyde Cooper died on February 12, 1998, short of a hundred. Holt told the Southern Foodways Alliance in November 2011 that she was fighting a developer's plan for a multistory apartment building on the Davie Street site — 'Ain't all about the money. It's about saving it for people and generations to come.' The building was lost; in 2014 the restaurant moved to South Wilmington Street, where the old awning hangs over the lunch counter and the old door hangs on the wall. In 2023, marking 85 years, Visit Raleigh noted it had at last begun taking credit cards.
how: Pork shoulders are trimmed by hand and cooked in the upstairs pits, then served chopped, sliced or coarse; the sauce is tangy rather than sweet, on Cooper's recipe. A tray — barbecue, slaw, hushpuppies and fried pork skins — cost $11 in 2023. Fried chicken, ribs and brisket, Brunswick stew, collards, boiled potatoes, several kinds of fried pork skins and banana pudding are the rest of the menu.
today: Open Monday to Saturday 10 to 6, at 327 South Wilmington Street, Raleigh, per OpenStreetMap (2026). Cards accepted since 2023.
address: 327 S Wilmington St, Raleigh, NC, 27601
geo: 35.77627, -78.63816 (street)
- kin → eastern-nc (style): its sauce leans east — tangy, vinegar-forward — though the meat is shoulder.
- kin → lexington (style): its cut is the Piedmont's, shoulder not whole hog; the tourism office calls the result a blend.
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): the cut, hand-trimmed, cooked upstairs.
- kin → pork-skins (dish): fried skins on the tray and by the bag, in several kinds; the thing regulars name.
- kin → barbecue-tray (dish): the $11 tray of 2023: barbecue, slaw, hushpuppies, skins.
- kin → brunswick-stew (dish): on the menu since the early years.
- kin → hushpuppies (dish): on the tray.
- kin → banana-pudding (dish): the dessert.
- kin → sam-jones-bbq (place): Raleigh's other barbecue name since 2021, a whole-hog house six blocks west on Lenoir Street.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): recorded Debbie Holt in 2011, mid-fight for the old building.

## Cook's Barbecue (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/cooks-barbecue/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/cooks-barbecue.json
id: cooks-barbecue
aliases: Cook's BBQ · Cooks & BBQ Still Smoking
facets: state=NC · status=closed · founded=1969 · fuel=wood · styles=lexington
region: The North Carolina Piedmont
what: A pork-shoulder pit off Valiant Drive south of Lexington, Davidson County, built by hand in 1969 by Doug Cook on a cul-de-sac plot down the road from his house — a pit and kitchen, a wooden chopping block, a drive-up window — with a dining room he framed from oaks felled on the lot. His son Brandon, born a year after the restaurant, came back as pitmaster in 2001 and kept the original brick pit and the hickory coals. In an October report DavidsonLocal recorded that the restaurant, by then trading as Cooks & BBQ Still Smoking, had announced on July 28 that it was closed indefinitely and would be sold; no reopening is on this disk.
story: Doug Cook built his stand in 1969 with his own hands; when customers wanted somewhere to sit he cut trees from the oak grove around it and framed a dining room. Brandon Cook grew up in the place — crawling into the fireplace as a child, flirting with the waitresses as a teenager — and learned under his father to tend the pits, shovel the cherry-red hickory coals and cook Lexington-style shoulders. He returned in 2001 as pitmaster and told the Southern Foodways Alliance's Rien Fertel in November 2011, 'Believe it or not, I'm related to half of the people around here that run the barbecue places, so yeah, I eat a bunch of it.' Customers dip their plates rather than pour sauce. DavidsonLocal, in an October roundup of Davidson County barbecue houses changing hands, reported that Cooks & BBQ Still Smoking on Valiant Drive had posted on July 28 that it was closed 'indefinitely' and was to be sold, with no buyer announced.
how: Shoulders cook over hickory coals in the original brick pit, the coals shoveled in from the fireplace; the meat is chopped on the wooden block and served Lexington style, with the dip beside the plate for dipping rather than poured over.
today: Closed. DavidsonLocal reported the indefinite closure and a planned sale; listings still showed it closed in September 2026 and no reopening is recorded on this disk. The building sits at 366 Valiant Drive, Lexington.
address: 366 Valiant Dr, Lexington, NC, 27292
geo: 35.7089148, -80.2732086 (street)
- kin → lexington (style): the style, in a one-family pit built by hand on the south side of town.
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): the cut.
- kin → brick-pit (pit): the original 1969 brick pit, still the one Brandon Cook tended.
- kin → hickory-and-oak (pit): cherry-red hickory coals, shoveled from the fireplace.
- kin → chopping-block (pit): the wooden block that was one of the three things the stand began with.
- kin → lexington-dip (sauce): served for dipping the plate, not pouring.
- kin → lexington-barbecue (place): the Monk pit across town; Brandon Cook counts himself kin to half the town's barbecue families.
- kin → bar-b-q-center (place): the Conrads' pit on Main Street.
- kin → rien-fertel (person): interviewed Brandon Cook for the Southern Foodways Alliance in 2011.

## Cooper's Country Store (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/coopers-country-store/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/coopers-country-store.json
id: coopers-country-store
aliases: Cooper's · Burrows's Service Station
facets: state=SC · status=open · founded=1937 · fuel=wood · styles=sc-pee-dee
region: The Pee Dee, South Carolina
what: A whitewashed general store on US 521 near Salters, south of Kingstree in Williamsburg County, that sells hardware, groceries, gasoline, diesel, propane, plow points, cast-iron cookware, live crickets — and, from a small meat counter at the back, whole-hog barbecue cooked over wood embers, hash, boiled peanuts and salt-cured country hams. Theron Burrows opened it as an Esso station in 1937; George Cooper built the pit after 1974; his nephew Russell Cooper has run it since 2003. It is a store, not a restaurant, and the barbecue is one more thing it keeps.
story: In 1937 the federal government built Highway 521 from Manning to Georgetown, and Theron Burrows, a tobacco and cotton farmer, opened an Esso service station and store on the new road. When he died in 1974 his daughter Adalyn and her husband George Cooper took it over as Cooper's Country Store. George watched families along the highway selling barbecue from car trunks and built his own pit — chickens on one half, hogs on the other. He ran the store twenty-nine years and in 2003 sold it to his nephew Russell Cooper, who told Rien Fertel of the Southern Foodways Alliance in June 2012: 'We keep all the meats. We keep all the hams. We got a full line of groceries and we got a full line of hardware. We got gasoline. We got propane. We got diesel fuel. You name it, we got it.' Garden & Gun sent Hunter Kennedy in 2014 and found the two-storey porte cochère over the pumps, the wood-panelled aisles, the plow points and cant hooks, and the Southampton-style country hams the same family has cured for the store for nearly sixty years, sold by the slice or whole and shipped across the country. A lunch buffet was added in March 2024.
how: Whole hogs cook over wood embers until the meat pulls with tongs; when the hog is flipped, the pitmaster Laverne Darby — more than thirty-five years at the pit — mops it with the vinegar sauce, which Russell Cooper describes as 'downright vinegar and salt and pepper', with black pepper, crushed pepper and ground red pepper. The hash is not ground but stringy, pulled meat cooked down. Barbecue and hash are sold from the meat counter at the back, with the hams, house-cured bacon, smoked tails and hocks; barbecue sandwiches and boiled peanuts too. The lunch buffet runs Wednesday to Saturday, 10:30 to 2.
today: Open Monday to Saturday, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., closed Sunday; lunch buffet Wednesday to Saturday, 10:30 a.m. to 2 p.m. 6945 SC Highway 521, Salters. The coordinates here are the highway at Salters Depot, not the building. Checked September 15, 2026 against Destination BBQ.
address: 6945 SC-521, Salters, SC, 29590
geo: 33.5938608, -79.8541999 (town)
- kin → sc-pee-dee (style): its style, in the store's own words: 'downright vinegar and salt and pepper' on a whole hog.
- kin → whole-hog (pit): cooked over wood embers until it pulls with tongs, for a meat counter rather than a dining room.
- kin → vinegar-pepper-sauce (sauce): its sauce — vinegar, salt, black, crushed and ground red pepper — mopped on at the flip.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): stringy hash, unground, from the meat counter.
- kin → barbecue-sandwich (dish): sold over the counter with the boiled peanuts.
- kin → browns-bar-b-que (place): the Kingstree buffet house seven miles north, the county's other whole-hog name.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): recorded Russell Cooper here in June 2012.
- kin → rien-fertel (person): interviewed Russell Cooper here in June 2012.
sources: s:web-sfa-coopers-country-store — Cooper's Country Store — Russell Cooper, interviewed by Rien Fertel, June 15, 2012; s:sfa-oral-histories — Southern Foodways Alliance oral history collection — barbecue projects (North Carolina, South Carolina); s:web-garden-gun-coopers-2014 — Our Kind of Place: Cooper's Country Store — Hunter Kennedy (December 2013/January 2014); s:web-destination-bbq-coopers — Cooper's Country Store, SC BBQ in Salters; s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina

## Dukes Bar-B-Que (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/dukes-bar-b-que/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/dukes-bar-b-que.json
id: dukes-bar-b-que
aliases: Dukes · Duke's Bar-B-Que · Dukes Bar-B-Que Whitman · Dukes Bar-B-Que Chestnut
said: Dukes, no apostrophe, on the family's signs; the Whitman Street site now writes Duke's.
facets: state=SC · status=open · founded=1955 · fuel=mixed · styles=sc-mustard
region: The South Carolina Midlands, South Carolina
what: The name on a dozen or more buffet houses across the Midlands and Lowcountry, all descended from the sons of Manuel Dukes of Orangeburg County, who learned pit cooking from a Rowesville pitmaster and catered the county's gatherings. In Orangeburg itself the line is Earl Duke's: he opened downtown at Chestnut Street and Columbia Road in 1955 and later moved to Whitman Street, and his sister's family runs a second Dukes on Chestnut Street. Both sell from a buffet line: chopped pork in a mustard-and-ketchup 'rust' sauce, hash over rice — the Midlands' stew of pork and onion — fried and barbecued chicken, and a loaf of sliced white bread at the end.
story: Manuel Dukes was born in rural Orangeburg County around 1875. His sons became the county's pitmasters, catering barbecues, and historians have suggested that their German descent explains the mustard in the sauce. Willie Baltzegar, a Rowesville pitmaster, taught them. In the 1950s the sons and daughters opened restaurants: Danny Dukes first, in Cope and Branchville; Earl Duke in Orangeburg in 1955, at Chestnut Street and Columbia Road, later moving to Whitman Street beside the Pepsi plant; a sister, Elma, and her husband Harry Ott on Spruill Street in North Charleston; and others in Aiken, Elloree, Smoaks, Ridgeville, Blackville and New Ellenton. The name spread past the family, and by 2017 some Dukes were family-owned and others sold. Earl's Whitman Street house passed to Harold Kittrell, a carpenter, and then to his son Tony, who told the Southern Foodways Alliance in June 2012 that 'the barbecue, hash, and rice, our sauce, sweet tea, and sliced bread are just what people come here for' and gave the sauce its name: rust gravy — sweet, ketchup-based, orange-yellow, thicker than most. The Otts opened in St. Matthews in 1965 and moved to Chestnut Street in Orangeburg ten years later; their descendants cook fifty to fifty-five pigs a week in the pit out back, Wednesday to Friday, for a buffet that is 'just barbeque, hash, rice and slaw with loaves of bread at the end'.
how: A buffet, all you can eat, paid at the register; in March 2011 the Charleston City Paper gave the price as $10 for adults and $6 for children. Chopped pork from shoulders and hams is dressed with the rust sauce; hash — pork simmered down with onion into a reddish stew — is ladled over white rice; fried chicken, barbecue chicken, collards, butter beans, black-eyed peas, mac and cheese, fried okra, hushpuppies, corn nuggets and a loaf of Sunbeam bread fill the rest of the line. Most Dukes houses stopped burning logs decades ago and cook on gas-fired cookers with wood chips for smoke; the Chestnut Street house cooks its hogs in a pit behind the building, and takes cash only.
today: Two houses in Orangeburg. Chestnut Street (789 Chestnut Street NE) opens Thursday to Saturday, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Whitman Street (1298 Whitman Street SE) lists Thursday to Saturday, 11 to 8, but its own site on September 15, 2026 reads 'temporarily closed. We plan to reopen soon.'
address: 1298 Whitman St SE, Orangeburg, SC, 29115
geo: 33.4903814, -80.8427238 (street)
- kin → sc-mustard (style): its style: the Orangeburg mustard belt, with ketchup stirred in.
- kin → mustard-sauce (sauce): its 'rust' sauce is mustard cut with ketchup — milder, sweeter, orange-brown.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): the dish beside the pork on every Dukes line.
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): chopped shoulder and ham, not the whole hog, at the Whitman Street house.
- kin → sweet-tea (dish): named by Tony Kittrell among the five things people come for.
- kin → light-bread (term): the loaf of sliced white bread at the end of the line.
- kin → gas-and-electric-cookers (pit): what most Dukes houses cook on now, with wood chips for smoke.
- kin → bessingers-bar-b-q (place): the other Orangeburg County family whose name went to Charleston.
- kin → maurices-piggie-park (place): the Bessinger chain from the same county; the Dukes stayed on the buffet line.
- kin → sweatmans-bar-b-que (place): the Holly Hill house, the county's other whole-hog name.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): recorded Tony Kittrell at Whitman Street in June 2012.
sources: s:wp-dukes-bar-b-que — Dukes Bar-B-Que — Wikipedia; s:web-sfa-dukes-bar-b-que — Dukes Bar-B-Que — Tony Kittrell, interviewed by Rien Fertel, June 4, 2012; s:sfa-oral-histories — Southern Foodways Alliance oral history collection — barbecue projects (North Carolina, South Carolina); s:web-city-paper-dukes-2011 — An Orangeburg family spawns a loosely connected barbecue empire across S.C. (March 2, 2011); s:web-destination-bbq-dukes-chestnut — Dukes Bar-B-Que on Chestnut St. in Orangeburg; s:web-dukessc-whitman — Duke's Bar-B-Que Whitman — official site; s:wp-barbecue-in-south-carolina — Barbecue in South Carolina — Wikipedia; s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina; s:web-destination-bbq-hash-map — The South Carolina BBQ Hash Map

## Fuzzy's Bar-B-Q (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/fuzzys-bar-b-q/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/fuzzys-bar-b-q.json
id: fuzzys-bar-b-q
aliases: Fuzzy's · Fuzzy's Barbecue
facets: state=NC · status=open · founded=1954 · fuel=wood · styles=lexington
region: The North Carolina Piedmont
what: A pork-shoulder house on Highway Street in Madison, Rockingham County, opened in 1954 by T.H. 'Fuzzy' Nelson and in the Nelson family since. Shoulders cook over hickory coals in pits behind the building; the tray is the Piedmont tray, chopped or coarse-chopped pork with the dip — the thin vinegar-and-ketchup sauce of the region — red slaw and hushpuppies. It holds True 'Cue certification, which turns on wood or charcoal being the only heat under the meat, and it is a stop on the North Carolina Barbecue Society's Historic Barbecue Trail. Breakfast is served from early morning, which few barbecue houses do.
story: T.H. Nelson, called Fuzzy, opened on the road through Madison in 1954, and the family kept it. The restaurant's own page calls itself a Nelson family restaurant operated by Fuzzy's son and daughter, Phil and Debbie, with Hilda Vestal managing after more than seventeen years; a visitor writing in April 2016 instead named a son, Fred, as the one running it, and the two accounts are not reconciled here. The building was rebuilt around 1978 and photographs of the first one hang inside. The pits stayed outdoors and the wood stayed in them. Both rosters of the Historic Barbecue Trail read for this project carry Fuzzy's — the older twenty-three-stop list and Visit NC's twenty-stop page of 2026 — which makes it one of the few pits to survive every revision of that list, while the Campaign for Real Barbecue certified it separately. *Inference —* the double listing is why Fuzzy's appears in nearly every written account of the trail, though its own advertising runs to one page and a telephone number. That page also claims notice from The New Yorker, from PM Magazine and from a Congressional barbecue contest. No issue, date or citation is given for any of the three, and none is repeated here as established.
how: Pork shoulders cook over hickory coals in pits behind the building, the fire tended through the cook rather than set and left. The meat is chopped or coarse-chopped and dressed with the dip; red slaw — cabbage cut fine and dressed with the same sauce, which is why it is red — and hushpuppies fill the tray. The kitchen serves breakfast from early morning as well, so the room is working hours before the barbecue houses down in Lexington open their doors.
today: Open at 407 North Highway Street, Madison. Three sources give three sets of hours: the restaurant's page says Monday to Saturday from seven in the morning and Sunday from seven, the NC Pork Council says Tuesday to Saturday from six and closed Sunday and Monday, and it lists a different street besides. Check before driving.
address: 407 N Highway St, Madison, NC, 27025
geo: 36.39363, -79.96889 (street)
- kin → lexington (style): the style of its tray: shoulder over hickory, the dip, red slaw.
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): the cut — shoulders only, as the Piedmont houses cook them.
- kin → lexington-dip (sauce): its sauce: thin vinegar reddened with ketchup, on the meat and in the slaw.
- kin → red-slaw (dish): the slaw on its tray, red because the dip dresses it.
- kin → hickory-and-oak (pit): its wood — hickory burned to coals in the pits out back.
- kin → campaign-for-real-barbecue (org): certified the pit as cooking on wood or charcoal alone.
- kin → north-carolina-barbecue-society (org): carries it on the Historic Barbecue Trail, on both rosters read for this project.
sources: s:web-fuzzys-bbq — About Us — Fuzzy's Bar-B-Q; s:web-truecue-nc — True 'Cue NC — certified pits; s:web-barbecuebros-nc-trail — NC Historic Barbecue Trail; s:web-visitnc-project543 — Cradle of 'Cue — the Historic Barbecue Trail; s:web-ourstate-historic-barbecue-trail — Running on Full: The North Carolina Historic Barbecue Trail (Bryan Mims, January 29, 2016); s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina

## Grady's Barbecue (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/gradys-barbecue/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/gradys-barbecue.json
id: gradys-barbecue
aliases: Grady's BBQ · Grady's Bar-B-Q · Grady's
facets: state=NC · status=open · founded=1986 · fuel=wood · styles=eastern-nc
region: Eastern North Carolina
what: A whole-hog pit at a country crossroads in Dudley, Wayne County, south of Goldsboro, opened on July 4, 1986 by Steve and Gerri Grady and run by Gerri and their son Scottie since Steve's death in August 2025. Hogs cook over oak and hickory coals; the barbecue is chopped by hand and served with stewed collards, cabbage, slaw and potato salad, and tea Gerri brews on the stove. The Assembly reported in February 2026 that it is, by most accounts, the one Black-owned brick-and-mortar whole-hog restaurant at the top of North Carolina's best-of lists, and one of the last of its kind. It opens four days a week.
story: Steve Grady's brother started the restaurant on a Friday in 1986 and quit by Saturday; he disliked the smoke. Steve and Gerri, married that same year, bought it with bank loans and the backing of the boss at the sawmill where Steve worked. Both had grown up on farms at Seven Springs. Steve had learned whole hog from his father and grandfather, who cooked a couple of pigs a year in pits dug in the ground for holidays; Gerri learned to cook at nine or ten from her mother and grandmother and then her mother-in-law, and told ABC11 in 2021, 'This is cooking the old fashioned way. It's a dash of this and a dash of that. There are no measurements.' Steve cut oak and hickory from storm-downed trees across Wayne County and stacked it beside the building where customers could see it. USA Today and GQ wrote the place up; the Gradys spoke for the North Carolina Barbecue Society and gave the Southern Foodways Alliance an oral history in December 2011. In June 2020 Steve was hospitalized with COVID-19; the restaurant reopened that July on its 34th anniversary. In 2024 the NC BBQ Hall of Fame and the American Royal both inducted him. Stephen Grady died on August 26, 2025; Gerri and Scottie kept the pit going.
how: Steve started the charcoal fires at eleven at night and came back at four in the morning to put the hogs on over hickory and oak; by eight the barbecue was ready. The meat is hand-chopped and dressed with a spicy vinegar sauce, and the plate carries slaw, hushpuppies — fried cornmeal fritters — and the day's vegetables, stewed collards, cabbage and potato salad, peeled and chopped by hand that morning.
today: Open four days a week at 3096 Arrington Bridge Road, Dudley, run by Gerri Grady and her son Scottie since Steve Grady's death in August 2025. Days and hours are from Our State (2013) and The Assembly (February 2026); check before driving.
address: 3096 Arrington Bridge Rd, Dudley, NC, 28333
geo: 35.2652434, -77.959773 (street)
- kin → eastern-nc (style): the style, cooked the way the Gradys' grandparents cooked it in pits dug in the ground.
- kin → whole-hog (pit): the cut, over oak and hickory coals from four in the morning.
- kin → hickory-and-oak (pit): its fuel, cut from storm-downed trees across Wayne County and stacked in view of the door.
- kin → hushpuppies (dish): on the plate beside the day's vegetables.
- kin → wilbers-barbecue (place): the other Wayne County whole-hog pit, on U.S. 70 the far side of Goldsboro.
- kin → scotts-famous-barbecue (place): Goldsboro's older Black-owned barbecue, closed now, whose sauce is still bottled.
- kin → north-carolina-barbecue-society (org): the Gradys spoke for it; Steve Grady entered the NC BBQ Hall of Fame in 2024.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): recorded the Gradys' oral history in 2011.
sources: s:web-ourstate-gradys — Grady's Barbecue — Our State (2013); s:sfa-gradys-barbecue — Grady's Barbecue — Stephen and Gerri Grady, interviewed by Rien T. Fertel, 7 Dec 2011; s:web-abc11-gradys — Grady's BBQ: How one of North Carolina's last whole hog barbecue joints survived the COVID-19 pandemic — ABC11 (24 Apr 2021); s:web-assembly-black-owned-bbq — N.C.'s Black-Owned BBQ Restaurants Are Keeping The Fire Alive — The Assembly (Nikki Miller-Ka, 13 Feb 2026); s:web-truecue-nc — True 'Cue NC — certified pits; s:web-barbecuebros-nc-trail — NC Historic Barbecue Trail

## Henry's Smokehouse (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/place/henrys-smokehouse/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/place/henrys-smokehouse.json
id: henrys-smokehouse
aliases: Henry's · Henry's Smokehouse BBQ
facets: state=SC · status=open · founded=1991 · fuel=wood · styles=sc-light-tomato, sc-mustard
region: The Upstate, South Carolina
what: An Upstate barbecue house at 240 Wade Hampton Boulevard on the edge of downtown Greenville, opened by Beau Hammond — in 1991 by the company's own account, in 1992 by the Greenville Journal's — in a small building that had been other eateries before. It cooks pork butts twelve hours and ribs six to eight over hickory logs in open pits, hand-pulls and chops the pork, and serves it with two sauces, a mild tomato-based one in the Piedmont manner and a spicy mustard one, with hash and rice on the side. A second house is in Simpsonville and a food truck, Henry's Hog Hauler, travels; the Barbeque Association lists it as 100-Mile Barbecue.
story: Beau Hammond opened Henry's with a menu so short that the sides were coleslaw and simmered green beans, and a rule he kept repeating: 'You want to be fair to the customer first. The money will come after that.' The house grew, added stores in Simpsonville and on Woodruff Road, and passed to Tiger O'Rourke and Bo Wilder, partners who added hand-cut fries in O'Rourke's years. Playboy ranked it first in the world in June 2002, a line the house still quotes; it took the Upstate readers' award seventeen years running; and in 2024 Southern Living picked it for the state. John Malik, writing in the Greenville Journal in October 2025, found a pulled-pork sandwich with fries and half-and-half tea at about $13 and the fire still built every day: 'You have to baby great barbecue. The fire changes every day... The result of great smoked pork should stay the same.'
how: Pork butts cook twelve hours and ribs, St. Louis cut, six to eight, in open pits over hickory logs — cured oak and pecan too, by Malik's account — at low temperatures, the fire built and tended all day. The pork is pulled by hand from the bone and chopped; the sauces are a mild tomato-based one and a spicy mustard; hash and rice, a stew of pork over rice, is on the menu with the hand-cut fries. About $13 for a sandwich, fries and tea in October 2025.
today: Open Monday to Saturday 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. and Sunday 11 to 3 at 240 Wade Hampton Boulevard, Greenville, with the same hours at 123 North Main Street, Simpsonville, per the company's site on September 15, 2026.
address: 240 Wade Hampton Blvd, Greenville, SC, 29609
geo: 34.86283, -82.38386 (street)
- kin → sc-light-tomato (style): the Upstate style it belongs to: pork butts, hickory, a thin tomato sauce beside the mustard.
- kin → sc-mustard (style): its second sauce is the Midlands' mustard, spicy.
- kin → light-tomato-sauce (sauce): its mild sauce, tomato-based, in the Piedmont manner.
- kin → mustard-sauce (sauce): its spicy sauce.
- kin → pork-shoulder (pit): pork butts — the upper shoulder — twelve hours over hickory.
- kin → hickory-and-oak (pit): hickory logs in open pits; oak and pecan by a 2025 account.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): on the menu, the Upstate's pork version.
- kin → pulled-pork (term): Henry's pulls the butts by hand, then chops.
- kin → lewis-barbecue (place): Greenville's Texas-style newcomer since 2022; Henry's is the older Carolina house.
- kin → home-team-bbq (place): the Charleston company's Greenville branch, since 2021.
- kin → midway-bbq (place): the Upstate's other old name, forty miles east in Union County, where the hash is beef.
- kin → south-carolina-barbeque-association (org): lists it as 100-Mile Barbecue.
sources: s:web-henrys-home — Henry's Smokehouse — official site; s:web-henrys-blog-2024 — Henry's Smokehouse blog (May 28, 2024); s:web-greenville-journal-henrys-2025 — Henry's Smokehouse remains an essential Greenville tradition — John Malik, City Juice (October 29, 2025); s:web-destination-bbq-henrys — Henry's Smokehouse on Wade Hampton in Greenville; s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina; s:web-truecue-sc — True 'Cue SC — certified pits
