## the pig that serves itself (art)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/art/cannibal-pig-sign/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/art/cannibal-pig-sign.json
id: cannibal-pig-sign
aliases: cannibal pig · suicide food · the self-serving pig · pig in a chef's hat
said: Nobody who paints one calls it anything. It is just the pig.
facets: kind=sign · state=both
region: The Carolinas, The American South
what: A barbecue sign on which the pig is not the meat but the staff: a pig in a chef's toque carrying a covered tray, a pig in an apron at a pit, a pig in sunglasses eating a pork sandwich, a pig holding the restaurant's own name over its head. The animal about to be served is drawn recommending the meal, and the joke is never explained on the sign because it does not need to be. The form runs from nineteenth-century trade cards to lit plastic on a bypass, and both Carolinas are full of it.
- kin → pig-mascot (art): the same animal without a job: a smiling pig that stands for the business but is not cooking, eating or serving.
- kin → roadside-barbecue-signs (art): the pylon the pig usually stands on, and the sign trade that put it there.
- kin → pigs-in-the-city (art): Lexington's painted sculptures, which take the upright pig and give it every job except this one.
- kin → maurices-piggie-park (place): whose West Columbia sign carries Little Joe, the best-documented Carolina example.
- kin → bessingers-bar-b-q (place): the Charleston side of the same family, and the same pig on its packaging.
- kin → maurice-bessinger (person): who put the pig on the sign and kept it there for half a century.
- kin → hog (term): the animal, drawn as a person, which is the whole trick.
- kin → barbecue (term): the word most of these signs spell Bar-B-Q, because the hyphens fit a pylon better.
- kin → political-barbecue-prints (art): the 1830s habit of drawing a pig with a part to play, which the sign painters inherited.
- kin → pig-pickin (event): the occasion a hand-painted plywood pig usually announces.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/images/cannibal-pig-sign/cannibal-pig-sign-pig-neon-sign-beale-street-memphis-tennessee-lccn2010630376.jpg · Public domain · Carol M. - image: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/images/cannibal-pig-sign/cannibal-pig-sign-bessinger-s-bar-b-q-sign-west-columbia-south-carolin-825aefd.jpg · Public domain · John Margolies · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABessinger%27s_Bar-B-Q_sign%2C_West_Columbia%2C_South_Carolina_LCCN2017709630.tif
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/images/cannibal-pig-sign/cannibal-pig-sign-bessinger-s-bar-b-q-sign-west-columbia-south-carolin-897b1ae.jpg · Public domain · John Margolies · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABessinger%27s_Bar-B-Q_sign%2C_West_Columbia%2C_South_Carolina_LCCN2017709631.tif

## How to order (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/story/how-to-order/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/story/how-to-order.json
id: how-to-order
aliases: what to say at the counter · ordering
said: The counter moves fast and the person behind it has heard every joke.
facets: kind=essay
region: The Carolinas
what: At a Carolina barbecue counter the words are short and they mean particular things. Barbecue is the meat, not the event. A tray has no bread; a plate does. Chopped, coarse chopped and sliced are three different textures off the same shoulder. Outside brown is the crust and you have to ask for it. This is the vocabulary, west and east, with what it gets you.
- kin → chopped (term): the word for how the meat comes off the block, and the three textures it names.
- kin → outside-brown (dish): the crust you have to ask for by name.
- kin → barbecue-tray (dish): what you get when you say tray: meat and slaw, no bread.
- kin → barbecue-sandwich (dish): slaw goes on the meat unless you say otherwise.
- kin → hash-and-rice (dish): the South Carolina order that changes the conversation.
- kin → barbecue (term): the word itself, which here is a noun for pork.
- kin → dip (term): the Piedmont's word for the sauce on the table.
- kin → lexington-barbecue (place): the Lexington counter where all three textures are on the board.
- kin → skylight-inn (place): the eastern counter where the menu is short and the answer is a tray.
sources: s:reed-holy-smoke — Holy Smoke: The Big Book of North Carolina Barbecue; s:garner-book-of-barbecue — Bob Garner's Book of Barbecue: North Carolina's Favorite Food; s:wp-barbecue-in-north-carolina — Barbecue in North Carolina — Wikipedia; s:moss-barbecue-lovers-carolinas — Barbecue Lover's the Carolinas: Restaurants, Markets, Recipes & Traditions
provenance default: tradition · confidence: medium · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## The Great Divide (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/story/the-great-divide/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/story/the-great-divide.json
id: the-great-divide
aliases: east vs west · the barbecue war · vinegar vs dip
said: Nobody in either camp thinks this is a matter of taste.
facets: kind=essay · state=NC
region: North Carolina, The Carolinas
what: North Carolina cooks barbecue two ways and has never agreed to disagree about it. East of Raleigh the whole hog goes on the pit and the sauce is vinegar, salt and pepper with no tomato in it. In the Piedmont only the shoulder goes on, the sauce gets ketchup and a little sugar, and the slaw turns red because it is dressed with that sauce. The argument between them has run in newspapers, been put to a vote in the General Assembly, and is conducted daily at lunch counters in both places.
- kin → eastern-nc (style): one of the two combatants: whole hog, clear vinegar, white slaw, cornbread.
- kin → lexington (style): the other: shoulders, red dip, red slaw, hushpuppies.
- kin → lexington-barbecue-festival (event): the festival the 2006 bills tried to make the state's own, and the 2007 act made the Piedmont Triad's instead.
- kin → jerry-bledsoe (person): the Piedmont's columnist, who called himself the world's foremost barbecue authority and meant it about half seriously.
- kin → dennis-rogers (person): the east's columnist, the oracle of the holy grub, who took the whole hog's side for decades.
- kin → red-slaw (dish): the fastest way to tell which side of the line a plate came from.
- kin → vinegar-pepper-sauce (sauce): the sauce the east will not add tomato to.
- kin → lexington-dip (sauce): the tablespoon of ketchup that started a war.
- kin → sc-pee-dee (style): eastern North Carolina's cousin across the state line, cooking the same hog with the same sauce.
- kin → sc-mustard (style): the answer South Carolina's Midlands gives, which neither North Carolina camp accepts.
- kin → adrian-miller (person): whose Black Smoke follows the cooks both camps forgot to argue about.
sources: s:wp-barbecue-in-north-carolina — Barbecue in North Carolina — Wikipedia; s:web-ncga-hb433-2007 — North Carolina House Bill 433 (2007): Lexington Barbecue Festival / Official Food Festival of the Piedmont Triad; s:reed-holy-smoke — Holy Smoke: The Big Book of North Carolina Barbecue; s:miller-black-smoke — Black Smoke: African Americans and the United States of Barbecue; s:wp-barbecue-in-south-carolina — Barbecue in South Carolina — Wikipedia; s:sc-parks-sauce-map — South Carolina Department of Parks, Recreation & Tourism — the four barbecue sauce regions
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Where all of this came from (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/story/free-to-use/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/carolina-barbecue/api/story/free-to-use.json
id: free-to-use
aliases: resources · open sources · how to check us
facets: kind=resources
region: The Carolinas
what: Everything on this site is built from things anyone can open: public-domain cookbooks, openly licensed encyclopaedias and photographs, open map data, oral histories published by the people who recorded them, and the directories that businesses list themselves in. This page is the list, so a reader can check the work or go further than we did.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): the archive most of the first-person material on this site comes from.
- kin → campaign-for-real-barbecue (org): publishes the list of certified wood-cooking pits this site reads the wood tag from.
- kin → north-carolina-barbecue-society (org): publishes the Historic Barbecue Trail, the other wood list.
- kin → south-carolina-barbeque-association (org): publishes South Carolina's trail and the four-sauce map.
- kin → adrian-miller (person): whose Black Smoke is the history behind half the directories on this page.
sources: s:web-feeding-america-msu — Feeding America: The Historic American Cookbook Project; s:web-wikibooks-cookbook — Wikibooks Cookbook; s:commons — Wikimedia Commons; s:web-greenbook-nypl — The Green Book collection, digitized; s:osm — OpenStreetMap — places tagged cuisine=barbecue in North Carolina and South Carolina; s:natural-earth — Natural Earth — Admin 1 States and Provinces, 1:50m; s:web-eatokra — EatOkra — a directory of Black-owned restaurants; s:web-black-restaurant-week — Black Restaurant Week — Southeast listings; s:web-wbenc — Women's Business Enterprise National Council — certified business directory; s:web-sba-wosb — Women-Owned Small Business federal certification and search; s:web-charlotte-lgbt-chamber — Charlotte LGBT Chamber of Commerce — member directory; s:web-blue-ridge-pride — Blue Ridge Pride — Asheville business and ally directory; s:web-afa-charleston — Alliance For Full Acceptance — Lowcountry; s:web-sc-pride — South Carolina Pride Movement; s:web-osm-lgbtq-tag — OpenStreetMap wiki — the lgbtq=* tag; s:sfa-oral-histories — Southern Foodways Alliance oral history collection — barbecue projects (North Carolina, South Carolina); s:true-cue — The Campaign for Real Barbecue (True 'Cue); s:ncbs — North Carolina Barbecue Society — Historic Barbecue Trail; s:scba — South Carolina Barbeque Association; s:miller-black-smoke — Black Smoke: African Americans and the United States of Barbecue
